references.text: Describes how Esau received the name Edom, which is relevant for understanding why his descendants are called Edomites.
Introduces Esau as Edom, directly linked to verse 19 where his descendants and their chiefs are summarized.
Introduces the genealogy of Esau, the ancestor of the Edomites in the Seir mountains, leading up to the summary in verse 19.
Summarizes the list of Esau's chiefs by name and place of residence, paralleling the summary in verse 19.
The verses form a literary framework where 36:43 expands on and completes the summary that begins in 36:19.
1 Chronicles 1:54 confirms and preserves the list of Edomite chiefs from Genesis 36.
The description of Ishmael's 12 chiefs in 25:16 forms a theological parallel to Esau's 12 chiefs in 36:19.
36:10 provides the specific list of sons that form the basis for the chiefs mentioned in 36:19.
36:8 establishes the settlement history as the foundation for the identity 'Edom' confirmed in 36:19.
1 Chronicles 1:35 confirms the names of Esau's sons, who are the ancestors of the chiefs in 36:19.
